references.text: David asks to be led on a path free from dangers and temptations, which resembles the prayer not to be led into temptation.
Jesus instructs the disciples to pray not to fall into temptation, reflecting the petition in Matthew 6:13.
Luke's version of the Lord's Prayer contains a similar request to be kept from temptation.

Hebrews speaks of Jesus as a high priest who can sympathize with our weaknesses and has been tempted in every way just like us, yet without sin, emphasizing the importance of praying to be kept from temptation.
James warns against giving in to temptation and explains how temptation works, offering insight into why it is important to pray to be kept from it.
In Revelation, protection from the global trial is promised to those who hold fast to their faith, which can be seen as a parallel to the prayer to be kept from temptation.
